Allow me to respectfully nuance a few of things you say here.

(i) My first paper on conscious AI, which was indeed sceptical, goes back to 2009 - long before the current hoohaa developed.  (See https://t.co/VCtZaYIrXJ)

(ii) I do not "need" biology to be vital to consciousness"   This is my current best guess. Based on my reading of  theory & evidence: (a) that computational functionalism (CF)  is likely false, and (b) biological naturalism (BN) may be true, but this is not yet demonstrated. My main goal is to know, which is why distinguishing between CF and BN (and other theories which take a position on conscious AI) is very important. In my BBS response I lay this out very clearly.

(iii) I do not think the word "caste" is helpful here, for reasons which should be obvious.

(iv) My time is limited and unfortunately I do not have the opportunity to debate with everyone (or every AI agent) who might take a different position.

Agree. Claude was able to do this better than I could since Opus 4.8 or so. 5.5 models are now very good at it.

All you do is give the model

1. a goal (eg. “Make p95 ci time <10 mins”)
2. a way to measure its result (eg. “Read timings in bigquery after each change”)
3. a sense of how hard to try (eg. “Don’t stop till it’s done, it might take a few weeks of experimenting”)

This pretty much works for most things. I often also ask the model to show me a chart with progress to goal every day, or to dm me a live artifact with the result

This feels like the next evolution of SEO/AEO that every product will try to game. Even if agents do the equivalent of ~10 hours of research on a product, it's less important on whether the product is actually better vs. the agent's perception that the product is better.

Companies will optimize for whatever preferences the top AI models have been posttrained on.

欧洲喊了这么久「主权 AI」，结果一个挺现实的案例是，欧洲本地平台开始托管 Qwen、GLM 和 Kimi 给欧洲企业用。

德国搜索引擎 Ecosia 今年 5 月才从 OpenAI 切到 Mistral，几个月后又换到欧洲平台 Melious 托管的开源权重模型。

欧洲想要主权、合规和可控，企业又要性能和成本，最后跑出来的方案很可能就是 开源权重 + 本地托管。

对中国模型来说，这可能也是一条很现实的出海路径。

比起「谁在榜单上更强」，谁能真的被欧洲企业部署进生产环境，可能更值得看。

reviewedPosts.author: Xudong07452910
reviewedPosts.text:
如果代码库里的每个文件都能自己解释、自己修改，还会提醒相关文件「你也得改」，Coding Agent 会不会更稳？

UIUC 和 Penn State 这篇论文提出 HERMES，把代码库里的文件、配置和测试变成一个个 Dev-Primitive。

可以把它理解成：每个组件旁边都有一个专门理解它的小 Agent。

遇到任务时，HERMES 先沿依赖关系找到真正相关的组件，只激活这一小部分。它们各自修改自己负责的内容，同时同步接口变化、配置约束和测试要求。

如果执行失败，系统会根据报错和测试结果，只重新激活相关组件继续修，不需要每轮重新读完整个仓库。

论文在 SWE-bench、仓库级重构、Terminal-Bench 和 DevOps 四类任务上测试，平均提升 12.4 个百分点。

还有就是把内部组件 Agent 换成 Qwen3-8B，整体只比全 GPT-5.6 Sol 方案低约 4.5 个百分点；在 Terminal-Bench 上成本还能下降 26.2%。

面对大仓库里的 Coding Agent，可能更需要一套稳定的「局部理解 + 协作修改 + 失败后定点修复」机制。

Harness 的价值也像是在组织代码、上下文和 Agent 之间的信息流。

📎 arxiv: https://t.co/GZBgGed7jM

reviewedPosts.author: Xudong07452910
reviewedPosts.text:
一个 Coding Agent，现在已经可以一次改上千个 PR 了。

Block 最近公开了他们怎么用 Claude Fable 5 做公司级代码迁移。

一次任务可以跨多个 Repo、几百万行代码。Fable 负责高层规划和拆解，再把具体改文件、跑测试这些工作分给更便宜的模型。

有意思的是人类工程师的角色也在往上移。

架构、数据模型、API 和关键设计决策留给人，机械修改和大规模迁移越来越多交给 Agent。Block 甚至已经让 Agent 定期扫描百万行级代码库，持续清理技术债。

所以当 Agent 开始能组织和维护整个代码库，Coding Agent 就越像一支软件团队，而不只是一个会写代码的助手。

Recently had the chance to interview @benhylak on how he is thinking about simulations in our AI Evals Course 😁

Simulations are incredibly useful for evals when you  do them well.  Ben discusses what he learned from implementing simulations for evals at several companies.  Some fun topics came up, my favorite being "simulation awareness" - when models know they are in a simulation.  

Below is a chapter summary:

02:02 Why input/output tests miss agent failures
10:59 Replay production traces to see what a change breaks
13:18 Recreate the data and tools around the agent
16:27 How agents detect simulations and change their behavior
20:39 Choose scenarios that test the change you made
22:00 Check answers, costs, and tool behavior across runs
26:43 Replay known failures to verify a fix
31:20 Common mistakes that make simulations misleading
32:20 Check that the simulation reproduces production behavior
37:37 When to start using simulations

You can also watch on YT here: https://t.co/EjlKZMw2y1
